_fixture.bug: E7d's fix to _pick_row (2026-08-15) requires only that a candidate row's own cells parse as money, dropping the old requirement that every column after the label parse. That is correct for a genuine trailing Confidence/Basis/Timing column whose cell is plain text ('High', 'Medium'). It is wrong when a descriptive column's cell states a dollar figure inside supporting prose rather than as the cell's own value: 'Basis' here reads '4-6% of CY2025 administrative payroll ($1.93M) [27]', and _money's old check (1 to 2 dollar-shaped substrings found anywhere in the cell) accepts it, because the parenthetical dollar aside is found the same way a genuine case value would be. The parser then reports two cases instead of one: the real 'Annual EBITDA Impact' figure, and a fabricated second case named 'Basis' worth $1.93M, a payroll figure with nothing to do with the impact estimate. This is the missing-vs-wrong failure the golden rule forbids: pre-fix, this row was correctly rejected outright (the 'Confidence' cell, 'High', fails to parse as money, so the old all-columns-must-parse check failed the whole row); post-fix it is wrongly accepted with a wrong number.
